name: Afghanistan
hint: Black, red, green vertical stripes with a white emblem of a mosque in the centre.
funFact: This is the flag recognised at the UN; since 2021 the Taliban government has flown a white flag with black writing instead.

name: Albania
hint: Red with a black double-headed eagle. Montenegro's eagle is gold, with a gold border.
funFact: Albania has over 170,000 concrete bunkers built during its communist era.

name: Algeria
hint: Green and white halves split vertically, with a red crescent and star straddling the middle.
funFact: Algeria is the largest country in Africa by area.

name: Andorra
hint: Blue, yellow, red vertical like Chad and Romania, but with a coat of arms in the middle.
funFact: Andorra has two co-princes: the President of France and the Bishop of Urgell in Spain.

name: Angola
hint: Red over black, with a yellow half cog-wheel and machete crossed under a star.
funFact: Portuguese is the official language, and Angola is one of Africa's biggest oil producers.

name: Antigua and Barbuda
hint: Red with a black, blue and white V-shape and a golden rising sun.
funFact: Antigua is said to have 365 beaches, one for every day of the year.

name: Argentina
hint: Light blue, white, light blue with a golden 'Sun of May' that has a face.
funFact: Argentina's name comes from argentum, Latin for silver.

name: Armenia
hint: Red, blue, orange horizontal stripes.
funFact: Armenia was the first country to make Christianity its state religion, in 301 AD.

name: Australia
hint: Blue with the Union Jack, a big seven-pointed star, and five white stars. New Zealand has four red stars.
funFact: Australia is the only country that is also a whole continent.

name: Austria
hint: Red-white-red horizontal. Latvia is darker maroon with a thinner white stripe.
funFact: Austria's flag is one of the oldest in the world, with legends dating it to 1191.

name: Azerbaijan
hint: Blue, red, green stripes with a white crescent and eight-pointed star on the red.
funFact: It's called the 'Land of Fire' for natural gas flames like Yanar Dag, a hillside that never stops burning.

name: Bahamas
hint: Aquamarine, gold, aquamarine stripes with a black triangle at the flagpole.
funFact: Christopher Columbus first landed in the Americas in the Bahamas in 1492.

name: Bahrain
hint: Red with a white zigzag of 5 points at the flagpole. Qatar is maroon with 9 points.
funFact: Bahrain is an island nation linked to Saudi Arabia by a 25 km causeway.

name: Bangladesh
hint: Green with a red circle placed slightly towards the flagpole. Japan's red circle is on white.
funFact: Bangladesh contains most of the Sundarbans, the world's largest mangrove forest and home of Bengal tigers.

name: Barbados
hint: Blue, gold, blue vertical with a black trident head in the middle.
funFact: Barbados became a republic in 2021, replacing the British monarch as head of state.

name: Belarus
hint: Red over green with a red-and-white folk-embroidery strip down the flagpole side.
funFact: Belarus shares the ancient Białowieża Forest with Poland, home of the European bison.

name: Belgium
hint: Black, yellow, red vertical: Germany's colours standing up.
funFact: Belgium has three official languages: Dutch, French and German.

name: Belize
hint: Blue with red stripes top and bottom and a detailed coat of arms showing two woodcutters.
funFact: It's one of the very few national flags that shows people.

name: Benin
hint: Green vertical stripe on the left, yellow over red on the right, and no emblem at all.
funFact: Benin is the birthplace of the Vodun (voodoo) religion, celebrated with a national holiday every 10 January.

name: Bhutan
hint: Yellow and orange diagonal halves with a white thunder dragon (Druk) holding jewels.
funFact: Bhutan measures success by 'Gross National Happiness' and absorbs more carbon than it emits.

name: Bolivia
hint: Red, yellow, green horizontal with a coat of arms. Ghana has the same colours but a black star.
funFact: Bolivia's Salar de Uyuni is the largest salt flat in the world.

name: Bosnia and Herzegovina
hint: Blue with a yellow triangle and a diagonal line of white stars, some cut off at the edges.
funFact: The triangle's three corners are said to stand for the country's three main peoples.

name: Botswana
hint: Light sky-blue with a black stripe edged in white across the middle, like a zebra crossing the sky.
funFact: Botswana has the world's largest population of African elephants.

name: Brazil
hint: Green with a yellow diamond and a blue starry globe with the words 'Ordem e Progresso'.
funFact: The stars show the sky over Rio de Janeiro on 15 November 1889, the day Brazil became a republic.

name: Brunei
officialName: Nation of Brunei, Abode of Peace
aliases: Nation of Brunei, Abode of Peace
hint: Yellow with white and black diagonal stripes and a red crest in the middle.
funFact: The Sultan of Brunei's palace is the largest residential palace in the world.

name: Bulgaria
hint: White, green, red horizontal. Hungary has red on top instead of white.
funFact: Bulgaria's 'Valley of Roses' produces a large share of the world's rose oil for perfume.

name: Burkina Faso
hint: Red over green with a single yellow star in the centre.
funFact: Its name means 'land of upright (honest) people', mixing words from two local languages.

name: Burundi
hint: A white X splits red and green triangles, with a white circle holding three red stars.
funFact: The three stars stand for the national motto: Unity, Work, Progress.

name: Cambodia
hint: Blue, red, blue with a white Angkor Wat temple, one of the few flags showing a building.
funFact: Angkor Wat is the largest religious monument in the world.

name: Cameroon
hint: Green, red, yellow vertical stripes with a gold star on the red middle. Senegal's star is green.
funFact: Cameroon is called 'Africa in miniature' because it has almost every African landscape and climate.

name: Canada
hint: Red, white, red vertical with a red 11-pointed maple leaf.
funFact: Canada has the longest coastline of any country.

name: Cape Verde
hint: Blue with a thin white-red-white stripe low down and a ring of ten yellow stars, one for each main island.
funFact: The islands were uninhabited until Portuguese explorers arrived in the 1400s.

name: Central African Republic
hint: Four horizontal stripes (blue, white, green, yellow) crossed by one red vertical stripe, plus a yellow star in the corner.
funFact: Its flag mixes French tricolour colours with pan-African colours to symbolise unity.

name: Chad
hint: Blue, yellow, red vertical, almost identical to Romania! Chad's blue is a slightly darker indigo.
funFact: Lake Chad has shrunk by around 90% since the 1960s.

name: Chile
hint: White over red with a blue square and a white star, a bit like the Texas flag.
funFact: Chile's Atacama is the driest non-polar desert in the world.

name: China
hint: Red with one big yellow star and four small stars curving around it.
funFact: China uses a single time zone even though it is wide enough for five.

name: Colombia
hint: Yellow, blue, red horizontal, with yellow taking up the whole top half.
funFact: Colombia is the world's leading producer of emeralds.

name: Comoros
hint: Four stripes plus a green triangle holding a white crescent and four stars, one per island.
funFact: Comoros is one of the world's top producers of ylang-ylang, a flower oil used in perfume.

name: Costa Rica
hint: Blue, white, a thick red, white, blue stripes, with a coat of arms on the red.
funFact: Costa Rica abolished its army in 1948.

name: Croatia
hint: Red, white, blue stripes with a red-and-white checkerboard shield in the middle.
funFact: The necktie (cravat) is named after Croatian soldiers who wore knotted scarves in the 1600s.

name: Cuba
hint: Five blue and white stripes with a red triangle and a white star.
funFact: Cuba is the largest island in the Caribbean.

name: Cyprus
hint: White with a copper-orange map of the island above two green olive branches.
funFact: Cyprus was famous for copper in ancient times, which is why the map on the flag is copper-coloured.

name: Czechia
hint: White over red with a blue triangle. The Philippines adds a sun and stars in its triangle.
funFact: Czechs drink more beer per person than any other country.

name: Denmark
hint: Red with a white off-centre cross: the original Nordic cross.
funFact: Denmark's flag, the Dannebrog, is the oldest national flag still in continuous use.

name: Djibouti
hint: Light blue over green with a white triangle holding a red star.
funFact: Lake Assal in Djibouti is the lowest point in Africa, about 155 m below sea level.

name: Dominica
hint: Green with a yellow-black-white cross and a red circle holding a purple Sisserou parrot.
funFact: Dominica is one of only two national flags with purple, thanks to its parrot.

name: Dominican Republic
hint: A white cross dividing blue and red squares, with a coat of arms that includes a Bible.
funFact: It's the only national flag that shows an open Bible.

name: DR Congo
aliases: Congo, the Democratic Republic of the
hint: Sky blue with a red diagonal stripe edged in yellow and a yellow star in the top-left.
funFact: DR Congo is the most populous French-speaking country in the world.

name: Ecuador
hint: Yellow, blue, red like Colombia, but with a coat of arms with a condor.
funFact: Ecuador is named after the equator, which runs through it.

name: Egypt
hint: Red, white, black stripes with a golden eagle in the middle. Yemen has no emblem; Iraq has green writing.
funFact: About 95% of Egyptians live close to the Nile River.

name: El Salvador
hint: Blue, white, blue with a triangle coat of arms circled by gold writing.
funFact: In 2021 El Salvador became the first country to make Bitcoin legal tender.

name: Equatorial Guinea
hint: Green, white, red stripes, a blue triangle, and a coat of arms with a tree and six stars.
funFact: It's the only country in Africa where Spanish is an official language.

name: Eritrea
hint: A huge red triangle stretching across the whole flag between green and blue, with a golden olive wreath.
funFact: Its capital Asmara is a UNESCO World Heritage Site for its Italian modernist buildings.

name: Estonia
hint: Blue, black, white horizontal stripes.
funFact: Estonia was the first country to offer internet voting nationwide, starting in 2005.

name: Eswatini
hint: A black-and-white Nguni shield and spears lying sideways across a wide crimson stripe.
funFact: Eswatini was called Swaziland until 2018 and is one of the world's last absolute monarchies.

name: Ethiopia
hint: Green, yellow, red stripes with a blue circle holding a yellow star. Green is on top.
funFact: Ethiopia's green, yellow and red inspired the 'pan-African' colours used by many African nations.

name: Fiji
hint: Light blue with the Union Jack and a shield showing a lion, sugarcane, a coconut palm, bananas and a dove.
funFact: Fiji has about 330 islands, and around 110 of them are inhabited.

name: Finland
hint: White with a blue Nordic cross, like snow and lakes.
funFact: Finland has around 188,000 lakes.

name: France
hint: Blue, white, red vertical. Italy swaps the blue for green.
funFact: France is the most visited country in the world.

name: Gabon
hint: Plain green, yellow, blue horizontal stripes.
funFact: Almost 90% of Gabon is covered in rainforest.

name: Gambia
hint: Red and green stripes with a blue band edged in white through the middle: the Gambia River.
funFact: The Gambia is the smallest country on mainland Africa and is almost completely surrounded by Senegal.

name: Georgia
hint: White with a big red cross and four small red crosses in the corners: the 'five-cross flag'.
funFact: Georgia is thought to be the birthplace of wine, with 8,000-year-old traces of winemaking.

name: Germany
hint: Black, red, gold horizontal. Belgium uses similar colours vertically.
funFact: Germany has more than 20,000 castles.

name: Ghana
hint: Red, yellow, green with a black star in the centre. The black star is the giveaway.
funFact: Ghana was the first sub-Saharan African colony to win independence, in 1957.

name: Greece
hint: Nine blue and white stripes with a white cross in the blue corner.
funFact: The nine stripes are said to match the nine syllables of 'Freedom or Death' in Greek.

name: Grenada
hint: Red border with six yellow stars, yellow and green triangles, and a nutmeg on the left.
funFact: Grenada is the 'Island of Spice', and the nutmeg on its flag celebrates its famous crop.

name: Guatemala
hint: Sky blue, white, sky blue vertical with a green quetzal bird and crossed rifles.
funFact: Guatemala's currency, the quetzal, is named after its national bird.

name: Guinea
hint: Red, yellow, green vertical: Mali flipped! Guinea starts with red at the flagpole.
funFact: Guinea has around a quarter of the world's known bauxite, the ore used to make aluminium.

name: Guinea-Bissau
hint: Red vertical band with a black star, then yellow over green.
funFact: Its Bijagós Archipelago of 88 islands is a UNESCO biosphere reserve.

name: Guyana
hint: Green with a white-edged golden arrowhead and a black-edged red triangle: 'The Golden Arrowhead'.
funFact: Guyana is the only South American country where English is the official language.

name: Haiti
hint: Blue over red with a white panel holding a coat of arms with a palm tree and cannons.
funFact: Haiti was the first nation founded by formerly enslaved people, independent in 1804.

name: Honduras
hint: Blue, white, blue horizontal with five blue stars in an X pattern.
funFact: The five stars stand for the five nations of the old Federal Republic of Central America.

name: Hungary
hint: Red, white, green horizontal: Italy's colours lying down.
funFact: The Rubik's Cube was invented by Hungarian Ernő Rubik in 1974.

name: Iceland
hint: Blue with a red cross outlined in white. Norway is the colour-swap: red with a blue cross.
funFact: Iceland has no army and is regularly ranked the world's most peaceful country.

name: India
hint: Saffron, white, green with a navy blue 24-spoke wheel. Niger has an orange circle instead.
funFact: By law, India's flag is supposed to be made from khadi, a hand-spun cloth.

name: Indonesia
hint: Red over white. Monaco looks the same but squarer; Poland is white over red.
funFact: Indonesia is the world's largest island country, with more than 17,000 islands.

name: Iran
hint: Green, white, red with a red emblem in the middle and tiny repeated writing along the stripe edges.
funFact: Iran was known to the world as Persia until 1935.

name: Iraq
hint: Red, white, black stripes with green Arabic writing ('God is great') in the middle.
funFact: Iraq was home to ancient Mesopotamia, where writing was invented over 5,000 years ago.

name: Ireland
hint: Green, white, orange vertical, with green at the flagpole. Ivory Coast is the reverse.
funFact: Green stands for Irish Catholics, orange for Protestants, and white for peace between them.

name: Israel
hint: White with two blue stripes and a blue Star of David in the middle.
funFact: The Dead Sea, on Israel's border, is the lowest point on land on Earth.

name: Italy
hint: Green, white, red vertical. Mexico adds an eagle; France swaps green for blue.
funFact: Italy has more UNESCO World Heritage Sites than any other country.

name: Ivory Coast
hint: Orange, white, green vertical: Ireland in reverse! Ivory Coast has orange at the flagpole.
funFact: Ivory Coast is the world's largest producer of cocoa beans.

name: Jamaica
hint: A gold diagonal cross with green and black triangles, and no red, white or blue.
funFact: Jamaica's is the only national flag without any red, white or blue.

name: Japan
hint: A red circle in the centre of white. Bangladesh and Palau put an off-centre circle on green and blue.
funFact: Japan is made up of more than 14,000 islands.

name: Jordan
hint: Black, white, green with a red triangle. The small white 7-pointed star on the red sets it apart from Palestine; no other flag in the region has it.
funFact: Petra, a city carved into rose-red rock, is one of the New Seven Wonders of the World.

name: Kazakhstan
hint: Sky blue with a gold sun, a soaring eagle, and a gold pattern down the flagpole side.
funFact: Kazakhstan is the largest landlocked country in the world.

name: Kenya
hint: Black, red, green stripes edged in white, with a red Maasai shield and two crossed spears.
funFact: Kenya is named after Mount Kenya, Africa's second-highest mountain.

name: Kiribati
officialName: Independent and Sovereign Republic of Kiribati
aliases: Independent and Sovereign Republic of Kiribati
hint: Red top with a golden frigatebird over a rising sun, and blue and white waves at the bottom.
funFact: Kiribati is the only country that lies in all four hemispheres.

name: Kuwait
hint: Green, white, red stripes with a black trapezoid (not a triangle) at the flagpole.
funFact: The Kuwaiti dinar is the highest-valued currency unit in the world.

name: Kyrgyzstan
hint: Red with a yellow 40-ray sun and a yurt roof (tunduk) in the middle. The rays were made straight in 2023.
funFact: The 40 rays stand for the 40 tribes united by the legendary hero Manas.

name: Laos
hint: Red, blue, red stripes with a white circle (the moon over the Mekong) in the middle.
funFact: Laos is the most heavily bombed country per person in history.

name: Latvia
hint: Dark maroon-red with a thin white stripe, darker and thinner than Austria's.
funFact: Latvia's red-white-red design is mentioned in a 13th-century chronicle.

name: Lebanon
hint: Red, white, red with a green cedar tree in the middle.
funFact: The cedar of Lebanon is mentioned dozens of times in the Bible.

name: Lesotho
hint: Blue, white, green stripes with a black Basotho straw hat in the middle.
funFact: Lesotho is entirely surrounded by South Africa, and even its lowest point is about 1,400 m above sea level.

name: Liberia
hint: Looks like the USA flag but with only 11 stripes and one big white star.
funFact: Founded by freed American slaves, Liberia became Africa's first republic in 1847.

name: Libya
hint: Red, black, green stripes with a white crescent and star on the wide black middle.
funFact: From 1977 to 2011 Libya's flag was plain green, the only single-colour national flag.

name: Liechtenstein
hint: Blue over red with a small gold crown in the top-left corner.
funFact: The crown was added after the 1936 Olympics revealed that Liechtenstein's flag was identical to Haiti's.

name: Lithuania
hint: Yellow, green, red horizontal, like a traffic light with green in the middle.
funFact: Lithuania was the first Soviet republic to declare independence, in 1990.

name: Luxembourg
hint: Red, white, light blue. The Netherlands is the same but with a darker blue.
funFact: Luxembourg is the world's only remaining Grand Duchy.

name: Madagascar
hint: White vertical stripe on the left, red over green on the right.
funFact: Around 90% of Madagascar's wildlife, including every lemur, lives nowhere else on Earth.

name: Malawi
hint: Black, red, green stripes with a red rising sun on the black top stripe.
funFact: Lake Malawi has more species of fish than any other lake on Earth.

name: Malaysia
hint: Red and white stripes like the USA, but the blue corner holds a yellow crescent and 14-pointed star.
funFact: Kuala Lumpur's Petronas Twin Towers were the tallest buildings in the world from 1998 to 2004.

name: Maldives
hint: Red border around a green rectangle holding a white crescent.
funFact: The Maldives is the world's lowest-lying country, averaging about 1.5 m above sea level.

name: Mali
hint: Green, yellow, red vertical: Guinea reversed! Mali has green at the flagpole.
funFact: Timbuktu in Mali was a great centre of learning, and its ancient manuscripts are still preserved.

name: Malta
hint: White and red halves with a small grey George Cross in the top-left.
funFact: King George VI awarded the George Cross to the whole island for its bravery in World War II.

name: Marshall Islands
hint: Blue with two diagonal stripes (orange and white) and a large 24-pointed white star.
funFact: Bikini Atoll, where the USA tested nuclear bombs, is in the Marshall Islands.

name: Mauritania
hint: Green with a gold crescent and star, plus thin red bands at the top and bottom (added in 2017).
funFact: The 'Eye of the Sahara', a 40 km wide rock formation visible from space, is in Mauritania.

name: Mauritius
hint: Four equal horizontal stripes: red, blue, yellow, green.
funFact: Mauritius was the only home of the dodo, which went extinct in the late 1600s.

name: Mexico
hint: Green, white, red vertical with an eagle eating a snake on a cactus.
funFact: The eagle comes from the Aztec legend of founding Tenochtitlan, now Mexico City.

name: Micronesia
hint: Light blue with four white stars in a diamond, one for each state.
funFact: On Yap island, giant stone discs called Rai stones, some 4 m wide, were used as money.

name: Moldova
hint: Blue, yellow, red vertical like Romania, but with an eagle coat of arms in the middle.
funFact: Moldova's Mileștii Mici cellars hold the world's largest wine collection, nearly 2 million bottles.

name: Monaco
hint: Red over white, the same colours as Indonesia but squarer. Poland is white over red.
funFact: Monaco is the world's second-smallest country, smaller than New York's Central Park.

name: Mongolia
hint: Red, blue, red vertical with a yellow Soyombo symbol on the left red stripe.
funFact: Mongolia is the least densely populated country in the world.

name: Montenegro
hint: Red with a gold border and a gold double-headed eagle. Albania's eagle is black.
funFact: Montenegro uses the euro even though it isn't in the EU.

name: Morocco
hint: Red with a green five-pointed star drawn as an outline. Vietnam's star is solid yellow.
funFact: Morocco's University of al-Qarawiyyin, founded in 859, is considered the oldest existing university.

name: Mozambique
hint: The only national flag with a rifle: an AK-47 crossed with a hoe on a book, inside a red triangle.
funFact: Mozambique's Indian Ocean coastline stretches about 2,500 km.

name: Myanmar
officialName: Republic of the Union of Myanmar
aliases: Republic of the Union of Myanmar
hint: Yellow, green, red stripes with one large white star across all three.
funFact: Bagan in Myanmar has more than 2,000 ancient Buddhist temples and pagodas.

name: Namibia
hint: A red diagonal band edged in white, a blue top corner with a golden 12-ray sun, and green at the bottom.
funFact: The Namib Desert is thought to be the oldest desert in the world, at least 55 million years old.

name: Nauru
hint: Blue with a thin yellow line (the equator) and a white 12-pointed star below it.
funFact: Nauru is the world's smallest island country and has no official capital.

name: Nepal
hint: The only non-rectangular national flag: two stacked triangles with a moon and a sun.
funFact: Nepal is home to 8 of the world's 10 highest mountains, including Everest.

name: Netherlands
hint: Red, white, blue horizontal. Luxembourg's blue is lighter; Russia goes white-blue-red.
funFact: There are more bicycles than people in the Netherlands.

name: New Zealand
hint: Blue with the Union Jack and four red stars outlined in white (the Southern Cross).
funFact: New Zealand was the first country to give women the vote, in 1893.

name: Nicaragua
hint: Blue, white, blue with a triangle emblem showing volcanoes and a rainbow.
funFact: Nicaragua's rainbow makes it one of only two national flags with purple (the other is Dominica).

name: Niger
hint: Orange, white, green horizontal with an orange circle in the middle. India has a blue wheel instead.
funFact: Niger is named after the Niger River, and about 80% of it lies in the Sahara Desert.

name: Nigeria
hint: Simple green-white-green vertical stripes with nothing on them.
funFact: Nigeria is Africa's most populous country, and its 'Nollywood' film industry is one of the biggest in the world.

name: North Korea
hint: Blue, red, blue stripes with thin white lines and a red star inside a white circle.
funFact: Rungrado May Day Stadium in Pyongyang is one of the largest stadiums in the world.

name: North Macedonia
aliases: The former Yugoslav Republic of Macedonia
Macedonia, The Former Yugoslav Republic of
hint: Red with a yellow sun whose eight rays stretch all the way to the edges.
funFact: Mother Teresa was born in Skopje, North Macedonia's capital.

name: Norway
hint: Red with a blue Nordic cross outlined in white. Iceland is the colour-swap.
funFact: The Nobel Peace Prize is awarded in Oslo every year.

name: Oman
hint: A red vertical band with a white emblem of crossed swords and a dagger, next to white, red and green stripes.
funFact: Sultan Qaboos ruled Oman for nearly 50 years, from 1970 to 2020.

name: Pakistan
hint: Dark green with a white crescent and star, plus a white vertical stripe at the flagpole.
funFact: K2, the world's second-highest mountain, is in Pakistan.

name: Palau
hint: Light blue with a yellow circle (the moon) set slightly off-centre.
funFact: Palau created the world's first shark sanctuary in 2009.

name: Palestine
capitalNote: Ramallah is the administrative centre; Jerusalem is the proclaimed capital.
hint: Black, white, green with a red triangle. It's like Jordan, but without the white star.
funFact: Jericho in the West Bank is one of the oldest continuously inhabited cities in the world.

name: Panama
hint: Four squares: white with a blue star, red, blue, and white with a red star.
funFact: The Panama Canal, opened in 1914, links the Atlantic and Pacific Oceans.

name: Papua New Guinea
officialName: Independent State of Papua New Guinea
aliases: Independent State of Papua New Guinea
hint: Split diagonally: red with a gold bird-of-paradise, and black with five white stars.
funFact: More than 800 languages are spoken in Papua New Guinea, more than in any other country.

name: Paraguay
hint: Red, white, blue horizontal with an emblem. The front and back of the flag are different!
funFact: Paraguay shares the Itaipu Dam with Brazil, one of the biggest hydroelectric dams on Earth.

name: Peru
hint: Red, white, red vertical: Canada's colours without the maple leaf.
funFact: Machu Picchu, the Inca citadel in the Andes, is in Peru.

name: Philippines
hint: Blue over red with a white triangle, a gold 8-ray sun and three stars.
funFact: It's flown upside down, with red on top, in times of war.

name: Poland
hint: White over red. Indonesia and Monaco are red over white.
funFact: Marie Curie, the first person to win two Nobel Prizes, was born in Warsaw.

name: Portugal
hint: Green and red with a yellow armillary sphere (a globe-like instrument) and shield on the dividing line.
funFact: Portugal and England have the world's oldest active alliance, dating from 1373.

name: Qatar
hint: Maroon with a white band and a 9-point zigzag. Bahrain is brighter red with 5 points.
funFact: Qatar's flag is the only national flag more than twice as wide as it is tall (11:28).

name: Republic of the Congo
hint: A yellow diagonal band separates green (top-left) from red (bottom-right). No stars or emblems.
funFact: Its capital Brazzaville faces DR Congo's capital Kinshasa across the Congo River, the closest pair of capitals after Rome and Vatican City.

name: Romania
hint: Blue, yellow, red vertical, almost identical to Chad. Romania's blue is a little lighter.
funFact: Bucharest's Palace of the Parliament is one of the heaviest buildings in the world.

name: Russia
hint: White, blue, red horizontal. Slovenia and Slovakia add a coat of arms.
funFact: Russia spans 11 time zones.

name: Rwanda
hint: A wide light-blue top with a golden sun in the top-right corner, above yellow and green stripes.
funFact: Rwanda banned plastic bags in 2008 and is known as one of Africa's cleanest countries.

name: Saint Kitts and Nevis
officialName: Federation of Saint Christopher and Nevis
aliases: Federation of Saint Christopher and Nevis
hint: A black diagonal band edged in yellow with two white stars, between green and red.
funFact: Saint Kitts and Nevis is the smallest country in the Western Hemisphere.

name: Saint Lucia
hint: Light blue with black, white and gold triangles: the twin Piton mountains.
funFact: Saint Lucia is said to be the only country named after a woman (Saint Lucy).

name: Saint Vincent and the Grenadines
hint: Blue, gold, green vertical with three green diamonds in a V shape.
funFact: The diamonds form a 'V' for Vincent; the islands are nicknamed 'the Gems of the Antilles'.

name: Samoa
hint: Red with a blue top-left corner holding five white stars (the Southern Cross).
funFact: In 2011 Samoa skipped 30 December entirely to move to the other side of the International Date Line.

name: San Marino
officialName: Most Serene Republic of San Marino
aliases: Most Serene Republic of San Marino
hint: White over light blue with a coat of arms showing three towers.
funFact: Founded in 301 AD, San Marino claims to be the world's oldest surviving republic.

name: São Tomé and Príncipe
officialName: Democratic Republic of São Tomé and Príncipe
aliases: Democratic Republic of São Tomé and Príncipe
República Democrática de São Tomé e Príncipe
hint: Green-yellow-green stripes with a red triangle and two black stars on the yellow.
funFact: It's Africa's second-smallest country: two volcanic islands sitting almost on the equator.

name: Saudi Arabia
hint: Green with white Arabic writing (the Shahada) above a sword.
funFact: Saudi Arabia's flag is never flown at half-mast because it carries the Islamic declaration of faith.

name: Senegal
hint: Green, yellow, red vertical with a green star on the yellow middle. It's Mali with a star.
funFact: Dakar, Senegal's capital, is the westernmost city on mainland Africa.

name: Serbia
hint: Red, blue, white stripes (Russia upside down) with a double-headed eagle shield.
funFact: Serbia is one of the world's biggest raspberry exporters.

name: Seychelles
hint: Five coloured rays fanning out from the bottom-left corner: blue, yellow, red, white, green.
funFact: The Seychelles' coco de mer palm produces the heaviest seed of any plant, up to 25 kg.

name: Sierra Leone
hint: Green, white, blue horizontal stripes. Gabon has yellow in the middle instead of white.
funFact: Its capital Freetown was founded in 1792 as a home for freed slaves.

name: Singapore
hint: Red over white with a white crescent and five small stars in the top-left.
funFact: Singapore is one of only three city-states left, along with Monaco and Vatican City.

name: Slovakia
hint: White, blue, red with a shield showing a white double cross on three blue hills.
funFact: Slovakia makes more cars per person than any other country.

name: Slovenia
hint: White, blue, red with a small shield showing a white mountain (Triglav) and three yellow stars.
funFact: More than half of Slovenia is covered by forest.

name: Solomon Islands
hint: A thin yellow diagonal stripe between blue and green, with five white stars in the top-left.
funFact: Guadalcanal, its largest island, saw some of the fiercest battles of World War II.

name: Somalia
hint: Light blue with one big white star in the middle.
funFact: Somalia has the longest coastline of mainland Africa, about 3,000 km.

name: South Africa
hint: A green sideways 'Y' shape with six colours: red top, blue bottom and a black triangle.
funFact: South Africa has three capitals: Pretoria (government), Cape Town (parliament) and Bloemfontein (courts).

name: South Korea
hint: White with a red-and-blue yin-yang circle surrounded by four black bar patterns.
funFact: South Korea has some of the fastest internet speeds in the world.

name: South Sudan
hint: Black, red, green stripes edged in white, with a blue triangle and a gold star.
funFact: South Sudan is the world's youngest country, independent since 2011.

name: Spain
hint: Red, yellow, red with a thick yellow middle and a coat of arms near the flagpole.
funFact: Spain's national anthem has no official lyrics.

name: Sri Lanka
officialName: Democratic Socialist Republic of Sri Lanka
aliases: Democratic Socialist Republic of Sri Lanka
hint: A golden lion holding a sword on maroon, with green and orange stripes on the left.
funFact: Sri Lanka is one of the world's biggest tea exporters, still sold as 'Ceylon tea'.

name: Sudan
hint: Red, white, black stripes with a green triangle on the flagpole side.
funFact: Sudan has more ancient pyramids than Egypt: over 200, at sites like Meroë.

name: Suriname
hint: Green, white, a wide red, white, green stripes with a yellow star in the middle.
funFact: Suriname is the most forested country in the world, with more than 90% forest cover.

name: Sweden
hint: Blue with a yellow Nordic cross.
funFact: Sweden's 'right to roam' lets anyone walk and camp on most land, even if it's privately owned.

name: Switzerland
hint: A square red flag with a white plus-shaped cross. It's one of only two square national flags.
funFact: The Red Cross symbol is the Swiss flag with its colours reversed.

name: Syria
hint: Green, white, black stripes with three red stars. This is the flag adopted in 2025.
funFact: Damascus is one of the oldest continuously inhabited cities in the world.

name: Tajikistan
hint: Red, wide white, green stripes with a gold crown under an arc of seven stars.
funFact: More than 90% of Tajikistan is mountains.

name: Tanzania
hint: A black diagonal stripe edged in yellow, with green top-left and blue bottom-right.
funFact: Tanzania is home to Mount Kilimanjaro, Africa's highest mountain.

name: Thailand
aliases: ราชอาณาจักรไทย
hint: Five horizontal bands: red, white, a wide blue, white, red.
funFact: Thailand is the only Southeast Asian nation never colonised by a European power.

name: Timor-Leste
hint: Red with a yellow and black arrowhead at the flagpole, and a white star on the black.
funFact: Independent in 2002, it was the first new country of the 21st century.

name: Togo
hint: Five green and yellow stripes with a red square and white star in the corner.
funFact: The five stripes stand for the five regions of Togo.

name: Tonga
hint: Red with a white top-left square holding a red cross.
funFact: Tonga's constitution says the flag can never be changed.

name: Trinidad and Tobago
hint: Red with a black diagonal stripe edged in white.
funFact: The steelpan drum was invented in Trinidad and Tobago in the 20th century.

name: Tunisia
hint: Red with a white circle holding a red crescent and star. Türkiye's crescent sits loose on the red.
funFact: The desert planet Tatooine in Star Wars was filmed in Tunisia.

name: Türkiye
hint: Red with a white crescent and star sitting right on the red. Tunisia puts them inside a white circle.
funFact: Istanbul is a major city that spans two continents, Europe and Asia.

name: Turkmenistan
hint: Green with a vertical red stripe full of carpet patterns, plus a white crescent and five stars.
funFact: The 'Door to Hell', a gas crater burning since 1971, is in Turkmenistan.

name: Tuvalu
hint: Light blue with the Union Jack and nine yellow stars arranged like its islands.
funFact: Tuvalu earns millions by leasing out its '.tv' internet domain.

name: Uganda
hint: Black, yellow, red stripes repeated twice, with a grey crowned crane in a white circle.
funFact: Uganda is home to about half of the world's remaining mountain gorillas.

name: Ukraine
hint: Blue over yellow: the sky above wheat fields.
funFact: Ukraine is the largest country lying entirely within Europe.

name: United Arab Emirates
hint: A red vertical stripe at the flagpole with green, white, black horizontal stripes.
funFact: Dubai's Burj Khalifa is the tallest building in the world at 828 m.

name: United Kingdom
officialName: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
aliases: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
hint: The Union Jack: England's red cross, Scotland's white X and Ireland's red X on blue.
funFact: The Union Jack appears in the corner of other flags too, like Australia, New Zealand, Fiji and Tuvalu.

name: United States
hint: 50 white stars on blue with 13 red and white stripes.
funFact: The 50-star design came from a 17-year-old's school project, which got a B-minus.

name: Uruguay
hint: Nine white and blue stripes with a golden 'Sun of May' in the top-left white square.
funFact: Uruguay hosted and won the very first FIFA World Cup, in 1930.

name: Uzbekistan
hint: Blue, white, green stripes separated by thin red lines, with a crescent and 12 stars.
funFact: The great Silk Road cities of Samarkand and Bukhara are in Uzbekistan.

name: Vanuatu
hint: Red and green halves split by a black-edged yellow sideways 'Y', with a curled boar's tusk on black.
funFact: Bungee jumping was inspired by Vanuatu's 'land diving' ritual on Pentecost Island.

name: Vatican City
hint: A square flag: yellow and white halves with crossed gold and silver keys under the papal crown.
funFact: Vatican City is the smallest country in the world, at just 0.44 km².

name: Venezuela
hint: Yellow, blue, red with an arc of eight white stars on the blue.
funFact: Venezuela's Angel Falls is the tallest uninterrupted waterfall in the world.

name: Vietnam
aliases: Cộng hòa Xã hội chủ nghĩa Việt Nam
hint: Red with one big yellow star in the middle.
funFact: Vietnam is the world's second-largest coffee producer.

name: Yemen
hint: Plain red, white, black stripes. Egypt has an eagle, Iraq has writing, Yemen has nothing.
funFact: Yemen's Socotra island has 'dragon's blood' trees found nowhere else on Earth.

name: Zambia
hint: Green with an orange eagle flying over three small vertical stripes (red, black, orange) in the bottom-right.
funFact: Victoria Falls, on the Zambia–Zimbabwe border, is one of the largest waterfalls on Earth.

name: Zimbabwe
hint: Seven stripes (green, yellow, red, black) with a white triangle holding the golden Zimbabwe Bird on a red star.
funFact: Zimbabwe is named after Great Zimbabwe, a medieval stone city whose bird carving is on the flag.
